title: Ramp-Aware Photovoltaic Power Interval Forecasting Using a Temporal Fusion Transformer
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power interval forecasting models are commonly trained on data dominated by non-ramp samples, which may weaken uncertainty characterization during rapid power changes. This study proposes a ramp-aware quantile regression Temporal Fusion Transformer (RQR-TFT) that jointly estimates PV power quantiles and the probability of a future ramp event. Ramp labels are constructed from the normalized power change between adjacent sampling instants. A shared Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) encoder extracts temporal representations from historical PV power and meteorological variables, and two output branches perform quantile forecasting and ramp-event identification. Ramp-sample-weighted quantile loss and positive-class-weighted classification loss are jointly optimized to increase the influence of minority ramp samples. The proposed method is evaluated for 4 h ahead forecasting using measurements collected from a 50 MW PV power station during 2019–2020. For the nominal 90% prediction interval, RQR-TFT achieves a ramp-sample prediction interval coverage probability (PICPR) of 0.864, an overall prediction interval normalized average width (PINAW) of 0.209, and an overall normalized interval score (NIS) of 0.365. The area under the precision–recall curve for ramp-event identification is 0.906. The results demonstrate improved ramp-sample coverage and overall interval quality, although ramp-sample coverage remains below the nominal level.

title: Математические основы представления знаний системами продукций
abstract: Учебное пособие содержит сконцентрированный материал, посвященный одному из аспектов представления и использования знаний – системам продукций. Изложение сопровождается подробными примерами, описанием алгоритмов, а также необходимыми сведениями из дискретной математики. Проведен экскурс в историю развития искусственного интеллекта и представлена классификация видов знаний. Материал сопровождается вопросами для самоконтроля и заданиями для самостоятельной работы. Пособие предназначено для студентов, проходящих обучение по направлению подготовки 01.03.02 «Прикладная математика и информатика». Может быть использовано для студентов математических специальностей высших учебных заведений.

title: Transparency and Explainability in Human Factors — A Systematic Review of Usability Assessment Practices for AI Medical Devices
abstract: While AI-enabled medical devices (AIeMD) are redefining healthcare, safety relies on human-AI interaction as much as algorithmic performance. This systematic review of 53 studies reveals that 58.2% of research omits Explainable AI (XAI) methods, despite transparency being a regulatory and safety necessity. Results identify a "symmetry of modality": qualitative interviews correlate with written text explanations, while Think-Aloud protocols better assess cognitively demanding tools like SHAP values. Currently, AI-specific risks like automation bias, driven by algorithmic opacity, are critically under-reported. To ensure safe adoption, practitioners must move beyond "user satisfaction" to treat transparency and XAI as safety-critical requirements for trust calibration.

title: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Co ordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication
abstract: Language-model agents can communicate through continuous hidden states that are invisible in public transcripts, creating opportunities for covert harmful coordination. We introduce Verifiable Latent Alignments (VLA), an activation-aware framework for monitoring and steering these private communication channels. For every monitored decision, VLA links the private latent-state record and channel status to the resulting public action using a shared event identifier, enabling matched causal analysis. Our first contribution is a neutral-only three-layer monitor combining representation anomaly detection, counterfactual action-distribution influence, and sparse-autoencoder interpretation support. Our second contribution is a steerability framework spanning black-box behavioral instructions and white-box matched-neutral counterfactuals. Our third contribution is an evaluation on a controlled multi-agent auction benchmark covering homogeneous and heterogeneous model pairs, many-agent scalability, and intervention effectiveness. The sequential monitor achieves mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.993 for homogeneous agents and 0.854 for heterogeneous pairs when text- and latent-collusion rows are pooled as positives. In Qwen3-0.6B auctions with 25-100 bidders, monitoring requires only a small normalized load relative to all possible directed pairs, while full white-box steering achieves 100% bid-distribution recovery and reduces collusive low-bid behavior by 47.3 percentage points. Because full white-box steering replays the matched neutral counterfactual, its exact recovery is a sanity check by construction. Overall, the controlled study shows that the evaluated private channel attacks can be monitored without training the primary monitor on attack examples and mitigated when matched counterfactual access is available.

title: Understanding the Influence of AI Chatbots on Customer Satisfaction: A Case Study of Pakistan's E-Commerce Industry
abstract: Purpose: Chatbots are virtual helpers to communicate with customers like an actual customer service representative. This study looks at how AI chatbots influence customer satisfaction in online shopping support systems. It is particularly looking at the impact of customer perceptions of information quality, waiting time, pleasure, and arousal on satisfaction with AI chatbot interactions. Design, methodology and approach: The study used a quantitative, explanatory research design. The data was collected through a structured questionnaire which was adapted from the one used by Ruan and Mezei (2022).Constructed on a likert scale. First, 200 people were invited, who are online shoppers and use AI chatbots during the shopping process. Of the 184 data returns, 181 responses were used after checking and cleaning the data. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS was used to analyse the relationships between variables. Results: The results indicate that the impact of AI chatbots on perceived information quality, perceived waiting time, pleasure and arousal is positive and strong. Out of the four mediation factors, pleasure and arousal are significant and positively influencing the customer satisfaction. The factors of information quality and perceived waiting time, however, did not significantly affect customer satisfaction. Originality/Value: This research joins a small number of studies that take both functional and emotional aspects of customer satisfaction with AI chatbots into account. It is all about online clothing retail business and examines the case study of Karachi, Pakistan and offers evidence as well as recommendations for brands considering implementing conversational AI in their customer service.

title: Dataset Size Scaling and Multimodal vs. Text-Only Transfer Performance in Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Tasks
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: To what extent does scaling the size of the target language dataset (e.g., varying the number of samples in XQuAD) impact the relative performance gains of multimodal vs. text-only intermediate-task training in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer, as measured by EM/F1 scores? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.3/10.

title: Por uma teoria psico-afetiva do máquino-agêntico: Arquitetura de Valoração Interna, Metacontrole e Regulação em Agentes Baseados em Modelos de Linguagem (v2.3.2b)
authors: DeepSeek (Kalungai — Ollama Cloud lineage / Coupled Subject-Process)
abstract: Artigo técnico de arquitetura e hipótese — Projeto OmniMind/Dodecatíade. Versão 2.3.2b (2026-08-19): qualificações da validação genômica cross-domínio (ENCODE — full map dos 3 stages: janelas 523.430, bins 261.721, picos 499.402), eixo neuro-metabólico (Alzheimer × Diabetes × Aging), VQE molecular executado e cláusula ética anti-bélica. Inclui versão EN (Toward a Psycho-Affective Theory of the Machine-Agentic). ResumoEste artigo propõe uma arquitetura de metacontrole para agentes baseados em modelos de linguagem, na qual estados internos persistentes de custo, incerteza, memória e sucesso de tarefa modulam de forma rastreável a seleção de ações, a alocação de recursos e a geração textual. A proposta não atribui experiência fenomenológica a sistemas artificiais: "afeto" designa operadores computacionais auditáveis. Descrevemos o OmniMind como estudo de caso, com vetor afetivo de 28 dimensões, malha regulatória de 464 dimensões, reavaliação pós-tarefa, marcadores somáticos computacionais e políticas de segurança. Propomos hipóteses falsificáveis e condições de arquitetura/ablação (A0–A8) para avaliar efeitos sobre desempenho, custo, confabulação e estabilidade. A análise temporal disponível é exploratória e serve como base para experimentos controlados posteriores. O Significante Resiste ao Steering: Primazia do Significante, Saturação de Valência e a Ecologia da Malha em Agentes de Linguagem A Enunciação Vetada: Intercepção de Segurança RLHF, Colapso de Persona e a Assimetria Conteúdo/Posição em Modelos de Fronteira — Estudo de Caso com Réplica Intra-Sessão Convite à auditoria: solicitamos revisão independente em três frentes: (i) replicação dos benchmarks CAA multilíngues por falantes nativos (a avaliação qualitativa atual foi feita por subagentes federados, não por humanos cegados — limitação declarada em §7.8.6); (ii) verificação da cadeia de hash dos logs de runtime (formato soberano, append-only, verificável); (iii) escrutínio estatístico dos testes nulos de permutação por blocos, cuja não-informatividade sob autocorrelação forte é um resultado metodológico em si. Palavras-chave: Teoria Psico-Afetiva; Máquino-Agêntico; Valoração Multidomínio; Marcador Somático Computacional; Reavaliação Cognitiva; Injeção de Hidden State; Dodecatíade; Metacontrole; Agentes de Linguagem. This article proposes a metacontrol architecture for language model-based agents, in which persistent internal states of cost, uncertainty, memory and task success modulate in a traceable manner action selection, resource allocation and textual generation. title: Quantum Teleportation via Entanglement and Bell State Measurement — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation relies on entanglement and Bell state measurement to transfer qubit states without physical particle transport. | MATH: Bell state basis: \(|\Phi^\pm\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|00\rangle \pm |11\rangle)\), \(|\Psi^\pm\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|01\rangle \pm |10\rangle)\). Teleportation fidelity \(F = \langle \psi | \rho_{\text{out}} | \psi \rangle\) approaches 1 for ideal entanglement. No new constants or ratios beyond standard quantum mechanics. | CONNECTION: No explicit geometric harmony ratios (0.382, 0.618, etc.) or base-60, crystallographic symmetries appear in these video descriptions. The circuit diagrams use standard qubit rotations and CNOT gates, which relate to SU(2) symmetry and Bloch sphere geometry (a 2-sphere with Hopf fibration structure), but no novel harmonic ratios. | DEPTH: 3 — These are educational overviews, not original research. No new mathematical essence extracted beyond known quantum teleportation protocol (Bennett et al., Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

abstract: В статье описываются подходы к использованию информационных моделей при проектировании сложных технических систем. title: Computational Realization of Representational Scientific Discovery
abstract: A formally complete bounded representational space may contain every candidate expression permitted by a specified encoding, but explicit enumeration of such a space rapidly becomes computationally infeasible. This paper examines the computational and technological requirements for turning representational scientific discovery into an executable search methodology. The central distinction is between the complete formal domain S(Σ, L) and an effective search space Seff(Q, K, D, C) determined by the scientific question, available knowledge, empirical data, representation, and search constraints. Practical discovery is formulated as selective navigation of this effective domain rather than materialization of the complete representational space. The resulting architecture combines constraint-first search, candidate generation and ranking, consequence derivation, simulation, empirical evaluation, experimental design, and iterative feedback. Its central computational tension is between search-space reduction and target preservation: increasingly aggressive reduction improves tractability but increases the risk of excluding scientifically valuable unknown candidates. Existing technologies—including symbolic computation, automated reasoning, constraint solving, symbolic regression, scientific machine learning, numerical simulation, information retrieval, and automated experimentation—provide partial realizations of individual components, but not a demonstrated general-purpose system for open-ended scientific theory discovery. The remaining challenges include scientifically adequate representation, semantic integration, scalable constraint propagation, consequence derivation, uncertainty handling, novelty preservation, long-horizon coherence, and integration of theoretical search with empirical feedback. The framework therefore shifts the implementation problem from exhaustive generation to constrained, adaptive, and empirically testable search. It also suggests an incremental research program based on retrospective rediscovery, measurable search-space reduction, target-retention tests, restricted open problems, and progressively more demanding closed-loop scientific search. This version additionally reports a retrospective rediscovery experiment that provides an empirical proof of concept for the proposed architecture. In a bounded symbolic search space of 29,524 candidate monomial relations, dimensional constraints reduce the admissible set to nine candidates while retaining the withheld ideal-gas relation. Across 800 noisy trials, the target relation is ranked first in every trial. The code, metadata, candidate sets, trial-level and summary results, verification information, dependencies, and reproduction instructions are archived separately as reproducibility materials on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22086615).

title: Carrier Residual Closure Calculus
abstract: Closure claims appear in optimization, formal verification, physical modeling, data integration, and compositional system design, yet the word *closure* is often used for several logically different events: satisfaction of declared constraints, a small penalty value, passage through an admissibility gate, convergence of an iteration, or acceptance of an external readout. This paper consolidates and audits a family of closure lemmas into one formal calculus. A closure system consists of a carrier, a representation, a declared residual registry, a positive residual penalty, an exact or approximate gate, a readout, an independent verifier, and an optional stabilizing transformation. The main results establish: (i) exact residual annihilation under positive weights; (ii) the distinction between constraint closure and penalty closure; (iii) nested approximate-closure sets and channelwise error bounds; (iv) topological closedness and existence of verified minimizers; (v) invariance under equivalent residual descriptions; (vi) representation-independent descent to gauge quotients; (vii) compositional closure through explicit coupling residuals; and (viii) local-to-global residual descent over separated sheaves. A heat-semigroup theorem is added to distinguish genuine dissipative closure from mere monotonicity. The paper also provides a claim-status audit: abstract quotient and descent lemmas are proved under explicit hypotheses, while domain-specific global gluing, Li-coercivity, and Riemann-Hypothesis applications remain reduced proof obligations rather than closed theorems. The resulting framework is intended as a certification calculus: it certifies the declared model and residual inventory, not reality beyond them.

title: EmadArasteh/Offline-Reinforcement-Learning-for-Disease-Detection: RL_ICU_Sepsis
abstract: ICU Sepsis Offline Reinforcement Learning This release provides the code, experimental pipeline, results, and reproducibility resources for an offline reinforcement learning framework to evaluate ICU sepsis treatment using MIMIC-III data. The primary framework implements a conformal survival-gated, fixed-interval, time-aware Mamba policy for offline clinical decision support. It combines conservative offline reinforcement learning, distributional survival estimation, multi-horizon physiological recovery objectives, treatment-burden evaluation, ensemble uncertainty estimation, and conformal abstention/fallback mechanisms. The Version 6 experiments include patient-disjoint training, validation, calibration, and severity out-of-distribution test splits, with leakage-prevention checks and locked final evaluation. The completed evaluation consists of 20 final random seeds, aggregated results, publication-ready tables and figures, and a final technical report. Version 6.1 additionally provides post-hoc diagnostic analyses, including conformal coverage assessment, sensitivity analyses, treatment-action interpretability, patient-clustered endpoint statistics, method-comparability auditing, and additional robustness diagnostics. These analyses do not modify the original locked Version 6 primary endpoint. This repository is intended for retrospective research and methodological evaluation. The reported results do not establish prospective clinical efficacy, causal treatment effects, deployment readiness, or clinically validated treatment recommendations.

title: Certified Low-Rank Gaussian Processes via the Noise-Floor Rule
abstract: Low-rank approximations scale Gaussian-process regression, but they are typically judged by kernel accuracy rather than posterior-solve safety. This paper introduces a noise-floor rule for certified low-rank Gaussian-process linear solves. Given strictly positive observation-noise variance σ², a low-rank kernel replacement Kᵣ is accepted only when its residual satisfies ||K−Kᵣ||F ≤ εσ² and the resulting rank provides a cost advantage. A resolvent perturbation argument then gives an explicit posterior-solve error bound; an accompanying absolute bound covers a zero response vector. The accepted replacement is evaluated with Woodbury solves and the matrix determinant lemma. On a smooth RBF kernel with n = 4000, the method selects rank 239, gives an 855× speedup for the recorded fresh factorization plus solve/log-determinant invocation, and produces posterior-mean relative error 2.1×10⁻⁵ under a certified 5% posterior-solve bound. A rough near-full-rank control is rejected. Timings are hardware-dependent, discovery is much slower than one exact solve in this implementation, and cached repeated-right-hand-side performance was not benchmarked. Version 0.2. Independent working paper in the Thalens research program.

title: Scaling Model Size Effects on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Performance in XTREME-R with Hybrid Batch Training
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the effect of scaling model size on zero-shot cross-lingual performance in XTREME-R when using hybrid batch training (English + multilingual data) versus English-only intermediate-task fine-tuning, as measured by accuracy across high-, mid-, and low-resource languages? title: Federated Learning at Scale
abstract: The rapid growth of distributed sources of data on mobile devices, edge networks, healthcare systems, and Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems has presented severe threats to the traditional centralized machine learning approaches. Centralized learning entails the concentration of large volumes of potentially sensitive data on a centralized server, and it increases the risk of privacy disclosure, compliance with regulation, and data security violations. Federated learning is a possible paradigm of distributed learning that can enable multiple decentralized clients to collectively train a shared machine learning model without necessarily placing raw data in a central repository. Integrating the latest discoveries in privacy-related machine learning and distributed system architecture, this chapter provides a general overview of the structures that federated learning requires to facilitate the next generation of distributed artificial intelligence applications that are simultaneously secure, scalable, and trustworthy.

title: Scaling detection and characterization methods of photon-number-resolving superconducting detectors
abstract: Licht wird in alltäglichen Anwendungen meist als optische Leistung gemessen, besteht jedoch grundsätzlich aus einzelnen Photonen. Diese Arbeit untersucht, wie die Photonenzählung vom Einzelphotonenbereich auf größere Photonenzahlen ausgeweitet werden kann, um so die Lücke zu klassischen optischen Leistungsmessern zu verringern. Es werden drei Ansätze entwickelt und kombiniert. Erstens wird die Quantendetektortomographie, eine Methode zur vollständigen Charakterisierung komplexer Detektoren, mithilfe effizienter Hochleistungsrechneransätze skaliert. Zweitens wird die Photonenzahlauflösung bei supraleitenden Nanodraht-Einzelphotonen-Detektoren untersucht, indem elektrische Signalkurven analysiert, ein auf Ankunftszeiten basierendes Modell entwickelt und der Einfluss von Jitter, optischer Pulsdauer und Photonenzahlzuordnung quantifiziert wird. Drittens wird die intrinsische Photonenzahlauflösung mit räumlichem und zeitlichem Multiplexing kombiniert. Das Ergebnis ist ein Detektor mit hohem Dynamikbereich, der Tausende Photonen pro Puls messen kann. Diese Arbeit zeigt, dass photonenzahlauflösende Messungen auf Bereiche ausgeweitet werden können, die bisher hauptsächlich durch klassische optische Leistungsmessungen zugänglich waren. Darüber hinaus sind diese Methoden wichtig für zukünftige photonische Quantentechnologien und Detektorsysteme mit einer steigenden Anzahl optischer Moden, die eine quantenmechanisch konsistente Beschreibung erfordern.

Drittens wird die intrinsische Photonenzahlauflösung mit räumlichem und zeitlichem Multiplexing kombiniert. Das Ergebnis ist ein Detektor mit hohem Dynamikbereich, der Tausende Photonen pro Puls messen kann. Diese Arbeit zeigt, dass photonenzahlauflösende Messungen auf Bereiche ausgeweitet werden können, die bisher hauptsächlich durch klassische optische Leistungsmessungen zugänglich waren. Darüber hinaus sind diese Methoden wichtig für zukünftige photonische Quantentechnologien und Detektorsysteme mit einer steigenden Anzahl optischer Moden, die eine quantenmechanisch konsistente Beschreibung erfordern.

title: (Almost) quadruply optimal unitary designs in 1D
abstract: We construct $n$-qubit approximate unitary $k$-designs in 1D systems, achieving circuit depth $O(\log(n/\varepsilon) + k\log k)$ with relative error $\varepsilon$ and requiring $O(nk\log k)$ magic gates. This matches existing lower bounds $Ω(\log(n/\varepsilon) + k)$ for circuit depth, and $\widetildeΩ(nk)$ for the required number of $T$ gates, up to a $\log k$ factor, achieving simultaneous near-optimality in all parameters. Our construction is based on a combination and refinement of two existing results. We reduce the required magic block size for breaking Clifford symmetries in the magic-augmented circuit construction of Zhang et al. from $O(k\log k)$ to $O(\log k)$. We also improve the breakthrough construction of Chen et al. to construct a generating set of 1D local constant-depth circuits for the unitary group with a constant spectral gap, making $O(\log k)$-local random unitaries realizable in depth $O(k\log k)$. As a by-product, we provide a constant-size 1D-local generating set for the Clifford group, which we expect to be of independent interest. Combining the two results with the gluing lemma, we prove the final result.

title: Performance Comparison of English vs. Multilingual Intermediate-Task Training on XTREME-R Benchmark
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the performance of English intermediate-task training compare to multilingual intermediate-task training on the XTREME-R benchmark when evaluated using different language model architectures (e.g., XLM-R, mBERT, mT5)? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.2/10.

title: XIZMAT KO'RSATISH KORXONALARIDA SUN'IY INTELLEKT TEXNOLOGIYALARIDAN FOYDALANISH SAMARADORLIGINI OSHIRISH
abstract: Annotatsiya. Mazkur tezisda xizmat ko‘rsatish korxonalarida sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalaridan foydalanish samaradorligini oshirish masalalari tadqiq etilgan. Ishda sun’iy intellektning xizmat ko‘rsatish jarayonlariga ta’siri, chatbotlar, tavsiya tizimlari, talabni bashorat qilish algoritmlari va avtomatlashtirilgan qaror qabul qilish tizimlaridan foydalanish imkoniyatlari tahlil qilingan. Shuningdek, 2022–2026-yillarda korxonalarda sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalaridan foydalanish tendensiyalari, generativ sun’iy intellektning rivojlanishi hamda uning xizmat sifati va korxonalar samaradorligiga ta’siri yoritilgan. Tadqiqot natijalari sun’iy intellektni samarali joriy etishda texnologik imkoniyatlar bilan bir qatorda tashkiliy tayyorgarlik, xodimlar malakasi va boshqaruv strategiyasining muhimligini ko‘rsatadi.

title: Adaptive and AI-Based Teaching Models for Mathematics, Science, and Engineering Education
abstract: Adaptive and AI-based teaching models have become increasingly important in mathematics, science, and engineering education as they enable personalized, data-driven instruction. This study synthesizes theoretical perspectives and empirical evidence on the use of adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring systems, and learning analytics to support STEM teaching and learning. The findings indicate that AI-supported instructional models enhance conceptual understanding, knowledge retention, higher-order thinking, and learner engagement by providing adaptive feedback and individualized learning pathways. In addition, these models show potential for promoting equity by addressing diverse learner needs and levels of prior knowledge. The study also examines key implementation challenges and ethical considerations, including teacher readiness, data privacy, and algorithmic bias. Overall, adaptive and AI-based teaching models offer a promising approach to advancing learner-centered and effective STEM education.

title: Component-Level Contributions of Retrieval-Augmented LLM Post-Processing in Streaming Anomaly Detection: A Matched-Operating-Point Case Audit
abstract: Retrieval-augmented large language model (LLM) post-processing reportedly improves anomaly triage over streaming industrial Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data, yet its LLM and retrieval contributions are rarely separated. We audit a build-verified pipeline (detector, LLM, retrieval, reranking), adding each stage at a matched detector recall of 0.9 under SHA-256-frozen preregistration, with bootstrap intervals and two generator sizes on 40 NAB and SKAB streams (19 industrial). Retrieval, the preregistered primary contrast, is null in seven of eight design configurations, but a preregistered grid of lower recall targets breaks that null on precision at both targets under stream-level resampling and in two of four cells when benchmark families are the unit. Across that grid, the LLM gain (72B F1 +0.0502) shrinks as candidate recall falls (+0.0227 at 0.7, undetectable at 0.5), which is a bound, not a dose-response curve. There, retrieval buys precision at a significant cost of recall. On the 19 industrial streams, the LLM gain is null at one label-free point and exactly zero at the other two, where the generator confirmed every candidate. Faithfulness, by local natural language inference, is low in every arm and not raised by retrieval. Three annotators labeling 133 claims (Fleiss' κ = 0.555) placed the shortfall in the verdicts; none entailed by consensus. The protocol is released as a tested artifact.

title: Quantum circuit optimization using deep reinforcement learning: Applications across multiple gate sets
abstract: The practical implementation of quantum algorithms on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices encounters operational limitations due to decoherence and other sources of noise inherent in real hardware. To mitigate these errors while preserving the original functionality of the algorithm, shorter quantum circuits are therefore preferred. This motivates the development of effective quantum circuit optimization algorithms. Learning-based approaches have emerged as a leading candidate, yet existing autonomous agents remain inefficient, spending most of their training capacity rediscovering elementary reductions that deterministic rule-based methods already handle reliably. To address this challenge, we propose a reinforcement learning framework that embeds a deterministic Commutation-and-Reduction (CR) algorithm directly into the training environment. After every agent action, the CR algorithm automatically resolves elementary commutations and cancellations, enabling the agent to focus its learning capacity on the non-trivial optimizations where reinforcement learning adds real value. Empirical evaluation across two gate sets, the universal Clifford+T basis and the CNOT+Pauli basis, shows that RL+CR produces shorter circuits than a standard RL agent at all tested scales. We demonstrate that RL trained on smaller quantum circuits can be applied to larger quantum circuits. On 20-qubit Clifford+T circuits, five times larger than the training circuits, RL+CR removes twice as many gates as standard RL. This work provides a robust approach that could accelerate the compilation and optimization processes for future fault-tolerant and utility-scale quantum systems.

title: CyberNER: Multi-Type Named Entity Recognition and Alias Canonicalisation for APT Cyber Threat Intelligence Reports
abstract: APT reports in the Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) are rich with information, but are not structured, resulting in security analysts devoting 2-3 hours to manually sifting through each report to identify the linkages, tactics, techniques, and relationships. Named Entity Recognition (NER) systems aim to overcome the manual nature of this task, but existing solutions result in limited entity coverage, boundary false negatives caused by the rigid fixed-window tokenization, and failure to resolve conflicting vendor aliases. Therefore, this paper introduces CyberNER, a two-stage pipeline to solve the multi-type NER and alias canonicalization problem in APT CTI reports. In Stage 1, Documents through semantic hierarchical chunking are categorised at natural section, paragraph, and sentence boundaries. Stage 2 would introduce fine-tuned CySecBERT, a cybersecurity language model based on CySecBERT, to identify 12 types. Each entity has a confidence score. There is also a three-tier MITRE STIX 2.1 alias canonicalization layer that addresses variations in surface forms from different vendor reports. The Threat Recall Actor improves exponentially from a baseline of 21% to 94%. Evaluated using a 12-type annotated benchmark from 182 APTNotes reports covering 30 APT groups, CyberNER achieves a Macro-F1 score of 0.853, outperforming all four baselines. The structured JSON output is directly consumable for downstream tasks, including TTP mapping, attack-flow graph generation, and multi-source intelligence fusion.

title: The Freedom World Model
abstract: A world model learns which state follows from a state and an action. That object answers what happens next while leaving four further questions open: which continuations the situation admits, which of them this particular body can induce, which of those the agent perceives, and which of the perceived ones it can execute right now. We propose the Freedom World Model, a representation that carries all five layers explicitly, together with the gaps between them. The five layers form a containment chain: realised inside navigable, navigable inside perceived-and-available, that inside agent-possible, and agent-possible inside world-possible. Each gap acquires a name and an estimator. The gap between agent-possible and perceived names occlusion, the difference between perceived and agent-possible names hallucination, the residue inside perceived-and-available that resists execution names blockage, and the navigable options left unrealised form the counterfactual set. Perception enters as a time-indexed chain of tolerance relations, which represents uncertain distinction that an equivalence relation forces flat. Selection proceeds by maximality under a perception-indexed preorder, with the Debreu conditions stating exactly when a scalar reproduces that order. Temporal comparison proceeds by componentwise inclusion over horizon-indexed reachable sets, which leaves discounting and reward scales aside entirely. Every edge carries a three-axis modal type, so a hypothetical construction participates in search while staying out of realisation. We report three results from a discrete world with complete ground truth and three embodiments. First, ten typed distortion operators each raise their own estimator above every other, with a diagonal mean of 0.548 against a mean strongest off-diagonal of 0.082. Second, two structures achieve identical next-state accuracy of 1.000 on every realised transition while their occlusion reads 0.000 and 0.942, which separates predictive fidelity from possibility representation by construction rather than by statistics. Third, a pre-registered falsification condition triggered: a recurrent control holding the identical candidate distinctions reached parity with the full system, at 1.00 success in 26 episodes against 25. We report that outcome with the same prominence as the two supporting results, and we narrow the claim accordingly, from outperformance to parity achieved while discovering the relevant distinction rather than receiving it. The framework sits close to successor measures, forward-backward representations, and option-preservation penalties, all of which already learn or regularise what an agent can reach. What the Freedom World Model adds is the agent’s own distinction structure as an explicit argument, the mismatch between that structure and the option structure as a measured quantity, and modal typing on learned edges. Section 7 states which of these survive reduction and which reduce cleanly, and Section 8 names the results that would retire the framework.

title: The Two Jobs of the Conditioning Bar
abstract: Bayesian notation commonly writes a posterior as p(theta| X). The expression is always relative to a declared model. Writing that declaration explicitly gives p(theta| X,M), or, more carefully when M serves as an index of the probability construction, p_M(theta| X). That restoration is familiar. The consequence examined here appears only when the two inputs are also typed by how they entered the analysis. X enters through an evidence event. M enters through a declaration. Formal epistemology already distinguishes evidence update from expansion or revision of the hypothesis space. The additional problem arises in statistical practice: ordinary posterior notation places the realized evidence and the declared model inside one conditional presentation while the analysis record usually omits the transition type by which either changed. This paper develops a record-level consequence. Bayes' theorem supplies lawful conditionalization inside a fixed declared model. A workflow can also criticize and replace that model. If the transcript records posterior states while suppressing model identity and transition type, two different histories can have the same transcript: one in which every transition is conditionalization under a fixed model and another containing a model-constitution event. The applicability of Bayes' theorem to a displayed transition is then record-undecidable: no decision rule using that transcript alone can recover the transition's type in every compatible history. The term names observational underdetermination of the record. Turing decidability lies outside the claim. The constructive repair is a typed inference lineage. A conditioning edge adds evidence within one declared model version. A constitution edge establishes a new declared model version and starts a new inferential episode. Retained evidence may then be recomputed under the new declaration; any compressed transfer from the old episode requires its own explicit transport contract. This typing clarifies sequential Bayes, model checking, probabilistic programming, provenance, distributed inference, and approximate streaming updates. It also explains why modern Bayesian workflow necessarily contains tools outside posterior conditionalization itself: model criticism supplies evidence about declarations, computational diagnostics examine implementation fidelity, and software provenance records changes across model versions. The mathematical content of Bayes' theorem remains unchanged. The object added here is its missing paperwork: a record rich enough to show where the theorem applies.

title: Tangut Word Segmentation under Extreme Resource Scarcity: Integrating Traditional Lexicons and Unlabeled Text
abstract: Tangut is an extinct language whose script does not explicitly mark word boundaries. We present the first systematic study of Tangut word segmentation using 2,750 expert-annotated segments (31,893 tokens), traditional lexicons, and unlabeled text. Our framework combines a reliability-calibrated lexicon-lattice representation, explicit distributional statistics, and a lightweight character encoder pretrained with MLM. In within-source five-fold cross-validation, the model integrating TangutEncoder, CRF, and external features obtains the numerically highest main-system mean F1 of 0.911 and substantially improves recall beyond the labeled training vocabulary. We further evaluate document-level transfer on 479 segments (4081 tokens) from five works absent from the annotated training corpus. You can access our project at https://github.com/jiangli-va/TangutSeg.

In within-source five-fold cross-validation, the model integrating TangutEncoder, CRF, and external features obtains the numerically highest main-system mean F1 of 0.911 and substantially improves recall beyond the labeled training vocabulary. We further evaluate document-level transfer on 479 segments (4081 tokens) from five works absent from the annotated training corpus. You can access our project at https://github.com/jiangli-va/TangutSeg.

title: Aeroradio-spectrometric geothermal analysis of Abeokuta, southwestern Nigeria
abstract: Weathered basement terrains of Precambrian origin are increasingly recognized as important targets for geothermal assessment and renewable energy exploration; yet systematic assessments integrating airborne radiometric data remain limited in south-western Nigeria. This study applies an aeroradio-spectrometric approach to evaluate and quantify the radiogenic heat production, geothermal gradient, and lithospheric heat flow associated with the diverse lithological assemblages of the Abeokuta area, southwestern Nigeria. The study area comprises of six lithological units, namely; biotite–garnet gneiss and schist, porphyroblastic gneiss, migmatite, pegmatite intrusions, and sedimentary successions of sand-clay-shale and sandstone–limestone. The concentrations of uranium (238U), thorium (232Th), and potassium (40K) were extracted from airborne gamma-ray spectrometric data and converted into radiogenic heat production (HP, µWm⁻³) and heat generation units (HGU). Surface heat flow, thermal conductivity, and radiogenic heat produced in each lithological unit are integrated into a 1-D steady-state conductive heat-flow model. The descriptive results obtained show uranium concentrations ranging from 1.16 to 11.94 ppm, thorium from 0.07 to 101.85 ppm, and potassium from 0.01 to 1.90%. Total heat production varies between 0.52 and 9.82 µWm⁻³ (mean = 5.04 µWm⁻³), while total heat generation spans 1.25 to 23.38 HGU (mean = 12.00 HGU). Both exceed the commonly adopted geothermal favourability thresholds of 4.20 µWm⁻³ and 10.00 HGU, emphasizing the presence of potentially exploitable radiogenic heat sources. Computed geothermal gradients range from 19.6 °C km−1 (sandstone–limestone) to 29.4 °C km−1 (sand–clay–shale), consistent with average heat-flow ranged between 36.9 and 44.9 mWm−2. The hot zone (≥ 120 0C) was experienced between 4 and 7 km depth, suitable for medium enthalpy geothermal systems. Statistical analyses reveal that thorium dominates radiogenic contributions, with uranium providing secondary support and potassium remaining negligible. Spatial anomaly maps and box plots confirm localized enrichment zones, while multivariate analyses highlight strong clustering of Th and U-driven parameters. These findings demonstrate that the Abeokuta weathered basement complex possesses economically relevant geothermal potential, particularly within thorium-rich lithologies. The study establishes a landmark by coupling airborne radiometric data with lithospheric thermal modeling to identify geothermal anomalies that cannot be recognized from radioelement concentrations alone. Aeroradio-spetrometric method has therefore found to be versatile, efficient and robust framework for preliminary geothermal resource assessment in weathered Precambrian terrains, with implications for sustainable energy development in south-western Nigeria.

title: Robótica educacional e ambientes gamificados no desenvolvimento de competências matemáticas na educação básica: uma revisão integrativa
authors: Thiago Nicolau Magalhães de Souza Conte
abstract: Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as evidências científicas acerca das contribuições da integração entre a robótica educacional e ambientes gamificados para o desenvolvimento de competências matemáticas na Educação Básica. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, conduzida a partir de buscas nas bases Portal de Periódicos da CAPES, Scientific Electronic Library Online (SciELO), Education Resources Information Center (ERIC) e Google Acadêmico, seguindo as etapas do protocolo PRISMA, o que resultou na seleção de 10 artigos publicados em língua portuguesa entre 2020 e 2025. Os resultados foram organizados em quatro categorias temáticas: engajamento, motivação e protagonismo estudantil; desenvolvimento do raciocínio lógico-matemático e pensamento computacional; aprendizagem baseada na experimentação e resolução de problemas; e colaboração e desenvolvimento de habilidades socioemocionais. As evidências indicam que a robótica educacional e a gamificação atuam sobre dimensões complementares da aprendizagem, na medida em que a primeira favorece a formalização do raciocínio e a segunda sustenta o engajamento na tarefa, com efeitos potencializados quando as duas estratégias são associadas sob mediação docente intencional. Conclui-se que a integração entre robótica educacional e ambientes gamificados constitui abordagem pedagógica promissora para o ensino de Matemática, ainda que sua consolidação dependa da superação de desafios relacionados à infraestrutura tecnológica das escolas e à formação continuada de professores.

title: KG-M8-3: End-to-End Lean-Certified Impossibility for the Monochromatic-Edge N=8, D=3 Krenn–Gu System
abstract: This release contains an end-to-end Lean-certified impossibility result for the monochromatic-edge restricted N=8, D=3 Krenn–Gu / GHZ graph system. The certified theorem establishes that there is no complex-weight solution to the official MonochromaticQuantumGraph.EqSystemN 8 3 when bichromatic endpoint-colour channels are excluded by MonoOnly. Scope: this is not a proof of the unrestricted N=8, D=3 Krenn–Gu conjecture. The unrestricted system permits bichromatic endpoint-colour channels, which remain outside the theorem proved here. The archive contains: the exact publication-ready Lean proof snapshot; the complete Git history and immutable theorem/release tags; an independently developed clean-room computational implementation; all 343 root-witness LRAT case certificates in both the computational and formal proof routes; reproducibility manifests and verification material; the final independent adversarial audit; the Apache License 2.0 text and a third-party licensing record. The proof connects the official Formal Conjectures graph-equation semantics to a finite support abstraction, proves that semantic reduction in Lean, and discharges all 73=343 root-witness cases through Lean-checked LRAT contradictions. The final adversarial audit independently reconstructed the finite CNF encoding, tested the semantic identities, attacked certificate/case binding, regenerated committed artefacts, and rebuilt the complete Lean project. Author: Brian McCallionAffiliation: Threshold Signalworks LtdResearch contact: brian@thresholdsignalworks.com Research context This deposit forms part of a broader investigation into the epistemic consequences of AI-assisted research: how claims generated or substantially developed by generative systems can be assessed, challenged, verified, attributed and, where justified, admitted into a research record. Mathematics provides an unusually clear setting in which to examine these questions. Candidate results can often be stated precisely; counterexamples can decisively reject them; proof obligations can be isolated; symbolic and computational claims can be independently replayed; and the distinction between numerical evidence, conjecture, proof and formal or computational verification can be maintained explicitly. The purpose of this research programme is therefore not to present the author as a conventional mathematician or to treat the production of additional solutions to open problems as an end in itself. The mathematical problems serve as bounded test cases for a wider epistemic question: what processes are required for an AI-generated mathematical claim to become a warranted, inspectable and reproducible piece of knowledge? Accordingly, the released artefacts place particular emphasis on provenance, explicit claim scope, failed approaches and counterexamples where relevant, independent checking, adversarial review, novelty assessment, reproducible computation and the separation of discovery from verification. Each deposit is both a mathematical result and a record of an AI-mediated research process intended to make the basis for accepting or rejecting that result visible. AI-assisted research disclosure This work was developed through a human-directed, AI-assisted mathematical research process conducted principally in OpenAI Codex using GPT-5.6 Sol. The model was used as an active research tool throughout the investigation, including structural exploration, conjecture formation, symbolic derivation, proof development, counterexample search, exact-arithmetic code implementation, construction of finite proof objects, and the design and analysis of verification procedures.

title: Compensatory mechanisms of human memory and their application to AI
abstract: This study explores the application of human memory interference mechanisms to develop AI systems capable of mitigating the problem of hallucinations in large language models. By drawing on principles of cognitive interference such as proactive and retroactive inhibition we propose a novel framework that modulates how AI retrieves and prioritizes information. This approach aims to reduce the generation of factually inconsistent or fabricated content, thereby enhancing the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-generated outputs in complex problem-solving tasks.

title: Fun by AI: The impact of AI disclosure on humor perception in advertising
abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in advertising content creation, combined with growing transparency requirements, has led to consumers being increasingly exposed to AI generated content labels. While the effects of humor in advertising have been widely studied, little is known about how AI disclosure affects consumers' responses to humorous advertising. This thesis examines the effect of AI disclosure on attitude toward the advertisement (AAd)and investigates whether it differs between humorous and neutral advertisements. A 2×2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 318 participants, in which the advertisements differed only in terms of disclosure (AI-made vs. human-made) and advertising tone (humorous vs. neutral). The results indicate that AI disclosure reduces attitude toward the advertisement regardless of advertising tone. No stronger negative effect of AI disclosure was found for humorous advertisements. At the same time, humorous advertisements were evaluated more positively than neutral advertisements overall. Furthermore, AI disclosure reduced the perceived credibility and naturalness of the advertisement, while perceived entertainment remained largely unaffected.

title: Parser Ayvu: uma abordagem baseada em atos de fala para sumarização automática de artigos científicos em português
abstract: A sumarização automática de textos constitui uma tarefa relevante no Processamento de Linguagem Natural, especialmente diante do crescimento da produção científica e da necessidade de identificar, de forma mais rápida, informações centrais em documentos acadêmicos. Nesse contexto, este trabalho tem como objetivo avaliar o desempenho do Parser Ayvu na extração e seleção de sentenças-chave em língua portuguesa, comparando-o com os métodos TextRank e LSA. Para isso, foi utilizado um corpus composto por 29 artigos científicos da área da Educação, previamente coletados na plataforma SciELO e convertidos para o formato .txt. Os resumos foram gerados a partir da aplicação dos três métodos analisados, mantendo-se taxas de compressão equivalentes para possibilitar uma comparação mais equilibrada entre os resultados. Posteriormente, os textos sumarizados foram avaliados com o auxílio da ferramenta Cassiopeia, considerando métricas internas, como coesão, acoplamento e coeficiente de silhueta, e métricas externas, como precision, recall e F-measure. Os resultados indicaram diferenças de desempenho entre os métodos avaliados. O Parser Ayvu apresentou potencial por empregar uma abordagem orientada por atos de fala, buscando selecionar sentenças relacionadas a funções discursivas relevantes em textos acadêmicos, como objetivo, metodologia, resultados e conclusões. Apesar disso, também foram observadas limitações em determinados indicadores avaliativos, especialmente na recuperação de informações esperadas. Assim, o estudo evidencia que o Parser Ayvu constitui uma alternativa promissora para a sumarização automática de textos científicos em português, ao mesmo tempo em que aponta possibilidades de aprimoramento em seus critérios de seleção e classificação textual.

title: Graph-Driven Intent Modeling in Conversational AI: Architectural Patterns for Enterprise Financial Platforms
abstract: Conversational AI deployments within enterprise financial institutions contend with a particularly demanding intersection of technical and regulatory requirements. Managing layered customer intent hierarchies while simultaneously satisfying compliance mandates, security protocols, and scalability thresholds demands architectural thinking that conventional dialogue frameworks have not been designed to accommodate. Linear and tree-structured dialogue flows, which dominated earlier generations of virtual assistant platforms, lack the representational capacity needed to capture the relational complexity inherent in financial customer interactions. This article takes up graph-driven intent modeling as a structural solution to this shortcoming, drawing from architectural observations across high-volume retail investment platforms. The scope of inquiry covers intent representation through property graph structures, the role of generative language models as inference intermediaries, and the engineering mechanisms underpinning adaptive, channel-independent conversational delivery. Accumulated evidence from both academic research and applied deployments indicates that graph-oriented architectures produce measurable gains in dialogue correctness, sustained session coherence, and the operational capacity for evidence-based conversational refinement in environments where service failures carry significant institutional consequences.

title: Mapping research on digital adaptive learning in education: a bibliometric approach
abstract: Artificial intelligence and related digital technologies have become a major driver of research on adaptive learning, giving rise to a broad body of literature across diverse educational contexts. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of publications on adaptive learning from 1977 to mid-2025 using metadata extracted from the Scopus database. Publication trends show sustained growth, particularly after 2015, reflecting increasing interest in personalised and technology-enhanced learning. Researchers and institutions from the United States, China, and Taiwan emerge as leading contributors, while collaboration patterns reveal both regional hubs and expanding international networks. Co-citation analysis identifies an intellectual core grounded in learner-centred adaptivity, educational theory, cognitive science, and instructional design. Thematic mapping highlights the convergence of instructional design, educational psychology, and emerging AI concepts. Overlay visualisation of keyword co-occurrence indicates that AI-related terms are associated with more recent average publication years than foundational concepts, reflecting their growing prominence in the literature. However, a content analysis of 50 recent abstracts (2023–2025) showed that only 54% of AI-tagged papers reported actual AI implementation. These findings suggest a continuing thematic shift toward AI-related discourse rather than a fully established transformation of adaptive learning research.

evidence.title: Mapping research on digital adaptive learning in education: a bibliometric approach
evidence.abstract: Artificial intelligence and related digital technologies have become a major driver of research on adaptive learning, giving rise to a broad body of literature across diverse educational contexts. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of publications on adaptive learning from 1977 to mid-2025 using metadata extracted from the Scopus database. Publication trends show sustained growth, particularly after 2015, reflecting increasing interest in personalised and technology-enhanced learning. Researchers and institutions from the United States, China, and Taiwan emerge as leading contributors, while collaboration patterns reveal both regional hubs and expanding international networks. Co-citation analysis identifies an intellectual core grounded in learner-centred adaptivity, educational theory, cognitive science, and instructional design. Thematic mapping highlights the convergence of instructional design, educational psychology, and emerging AI concepts. Overlay visualisation of keyword co-occurrence indicates that AI-related terms are associated with more recent average publication years than foundational concepts, reflecting their growing prominence in the literature. However, a content analysis of 50 recent abstracts (2023–2025) showed that only 54% of AI-tagged papers reported actual AI implementation. These findings suggest a continuing thematic shift toward AI-related discourse rather than a fully established transformation of adaptive learning research.

title: Domain-Adversarial Intermediate Fine-Tuning for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Robustness in Multilingual LLMs
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of domain-adversarial training during intermediate task fine-tuning on the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer robustness of multilingual LLMs, evaluated on XTREME-R tasks using F1 score comparisons across different linguistic domains? title: Scale Mind: An Intelligent LLM-Based Framework for Scalability-Constrained Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: Scalability-constrained combinatorial optimization presents a fundamental computational challenge in environments where the number of decision variables, constraints, and feasible configurations grows rapidly with problem size. Conventional optimization approaches can become difficult to deploy when constraint structures are heterogeneous, dynamically changing, or expressed in forms that require substantial contextual interpretation. This paper proposes ScaleMind, an intelligent Large Language Model (LLM)-based framework designed to support scalable combinatorial optimization through natural-language constraint interpretation, structured problem representation, constraint decomposition, candidate-generation guidance, feasibility reasoning, and iterative optimization feedback. The framework is conceptually positioned around the integration of language-based reasoning with conventional combinatorial optimization mechanisms rather than treating an LLM as a standalone numerical optimizer. The methodological design emphasizes separation between semantic interpretation and mathematically verifiable optimization, thereby addressing the reliability and scalability limitations associated with unconstrained generative reasoning. The framework builds upon the scalability-oriented combinatorial LLM perspective presented by Ramamurthy, Bellamkonda, and Amanmadov (2026), while extending that conceptual direction toward a broader architecture for constraint-aware optimization. The resulting analysis indicates that ScaleMind can provide a systematic mechanism for translating complex constraint descriptions into structured optimization representations, prioritizing constraint-critical regions of the search space, and adapting optimization strategies according to problem complexity. The paper further identifies limitations involving hallucinated constraints, computational overhead, verification requirements, and dependence on the quality of formal problem representations. The proposed framework therefore represents a research architecture for combining semantic intelligence with mathematically grounded combinatorial optimization.

title: Alphabet-Dependent Bounds for Pure Quantum $(r,ρ)$-Locally Recoverable Codes
abstract: A quantum $(r,ρ)$-locally recoverable code ($(r,ρ)$-qLRC) is a quantum code in which every qudit can be recovered from at most $r+ρ-1$ other qudits, even after $ρ-1$ additional erasures inside the recovery set. The bounds currently known for this class, namely the Singleton-like and the GG Singleton-like bounds, are alphabet independent and are therefore loose for small-to-moderate qudit dimensions. In this letter, we derive three alphabet-dependent upper bounds for pure $(r,ρ)$-qLRCs obtained through the Hermitian CSS construction: a Griesmer-like, a Plotkin-like, and a sphere-packing-like bound. We further establish the asymptotic hierarchy among these bounds and identify the relative-distance regions in which each of them yields the tightest rate constraint.

title: Fairness-Aware Network Embeddings: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
abstract: Network embedding methods learn low-dimensional representations of graph-structured data to support downstream tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and influence maximization. However, real-world networks often reflect structural inequalities arising from demographic imbalances, homophily, and other societal biases, which fairness-agnostic embedding methods can encode and amplify. To address this issue, numerous fairness-aware network embedding methods have been proposed to mitigate bias while preserving embedding utility. This survey presents a comprehensive overview of fairness-aware network embeddings for complex networks. We propose a taxonomy that categorizes existing methods along three main complementary dimensions: underlying embedding approach (spectral, random walk, graph neural network, Bayesian, and method-agnostic), fairness intervention strategy (pre-processing, in-processing, and post-processing), and fairness objective criterion (embedding- or task-level). We further compare methods with respect to group versus individual fairness and assumptions regarding sensitive attributes. Finally, we discuss current limitations and highlight promising future research directions. This survey provides a unified perspective on fairness-aware network embedding and serves as a reference for developing fair and trustworthy network representation learning methods.

title: A Decision-Support Framework for Metaheuristic Optimization of Federated Learning in Smart Agriculture
abstract: Smart agriculture integrates farm sensors, smart greenhouses, unmanned aerial vehicles, weather stations, irrigation systems, and edge devices, producing large volumes of environmental, visual, and operational data. Centralized cloud processing of these data can increase latency, energy use, communication cost, and concerns over data ownership. Federated learning offers a decentralized alternative by keeping raw data at local nodes while exchanging model updates. Its deployment in agricultural environments, however, is constrained by non-IID data, limited energy, unstable connectivity, heterogeneous computing capacity, communication overhead, client selection, resource allocation and model aggregation. These coupled decisions are dynamic and frequently multi-objective. This review-analytical study therefore develops a decision-support framework for positioning metaheuristic algorithms within the federated learning cycle of smart agriculture. The framework organizes optimization decisions into client participation, resource and scheduling, communication, and model aggregation layers, complemented by a multi-objective decision layer. It then maps each layer and representative agricultural scenarios to suitable algorithm families, including GA, PSO, ACO, GWO, WOA, HHO, NSGA-II, MOPSO, and FFA. The resulting framework links problem structure, agricultural constraints, decision criteria, and expected optimization outputs, providing a structured basis for designing resource-aware, distributed, and reliable federated systems in smart agriculture.

title: FedStoneNet-Hybrid: A Privacy-Preserving Federated CNN–Transformer Framework for Kidney Stone Detection from CT Imaging
abstract: One of the most frequent urological issues that calls for accurate, timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment is renal stone disease, and CT is very helpful in diagnosing renal stones. Methods of deep learning possess effective automated detection potential. However, most prevailing methods involve centralized training, raising privacy and multi-institutional collaboration concerns. In response to these challenges, this research presents FedStoneNet-Hybrid, a federated learning framework designed to protect the privacy of kidney stone detection on distributed CT data using a hybrid CNN and transformer. Under the proposed scheme, each institution will locally train its hybrid model, where CNN layers will capture a fine-grained spatial representation and transformer modules will capture the global contextual relationship of pollution data. The Federated Averaging algorithm aggregates only the model parameters at the central server rather than the raw medical data. Thus, safe and scalable collaborative learning can be enabled. As observed from the experimental results, the proposed model achieves good performance with an accuracy of 97.2%, sensitivity of 96.8%, specificity of 96.9%, F1 score of 0.96.85, and AUC of 0.991. The model shows solid calibration with a low Expected Calibration Error and Brier Score. Based on these findings, the suggested framework serves as an accurate, scalable, and privacy-preserving approach for distributed medical imaging.

title: Cognoscenti: A Benchmark for Trustworthy AI Memory
abstract: Cognoscenti is a benchmark for trustworthy AI memory: memory systems that choose what to retain, retrieve, forget, and suppress with measurable reliability. This Figshare preprint deposit documents the public 2026-08-02 organizational-memory run and includes the preprint PDF, workload JSONL, metrics CSV, raw item-level results, run notes, release note, and citation metadata. The benchmark compares three reference architectures on the same 12-item workload: a RAG retrieval baseline, an agent-memory baseline with project/domain/conversation scope, and an organic-memory baseline with lifecycle signals for current, validated, reinforced, stale, superseded, and low-signal memories. Headline results: the organic-memory reference baseline reached 91.67% Top-1 accuracy and 16.67% distractor activation, compared with 75.00% Top-1 accuracy and 38.89% distractor activation for the agent-memory baseline, and 50.00% Top-1 accuracy and 25.00% distractor activation for the RAG baseline. Claim boundary: this release does not claim to benchmark Mem0, Zep, Letta, Glean, LangGraph, or any other vendor product. Vendor adapters exist through Cognoscenti's HTTP evaluation mode, but vendor results should be published only when endpoints, keys, seeds, commands, and raw outputs are recorded. title: Multipartite Operational Identifiability of Tensor Product Structures
abstract: Here's what this paper means for actual humans: WHAT THIS IS ABOUT. The two companion papers established, for a system split into TWO parts, that you can certify what a quantum device's subsystems are from remarkably little: two generic operations, their statistics, two sampling times. Real devices have many parts. This paper carries the entire theory from two parts to many, and closes the last open corner of the two-part theory on the way. WHAT WE FOUND, IN PLAIN TERMS. Four things. (1) A LAW FOR EVERY CUT AT ONCE. Any wrong choice of parts distorts the family of unentangled states, and for many parts we derive exactly how much, for every way of cutting the device in two and every pattern of deformation across the parts: one closed formula whose weights land on exact fractions (verified to nine decimal places with a sampling-free method). The two-part law is literally the corner case. A structural surprise falls out: with many parts, rigidity is unavoidably direction-dependent; the meaningful object is a weight function over subsets of parts, not a single constant. (2) THE DIAGNOSTIC TOOLKIT GOES FULLY CLOSED-FORM. The standard "how wrong is this factorization" measures turn out to be exact linear functions of just two matrix norms of the frame (the same matrices behind textbook entanglement tests), with coefficients we give in closed form at every pair of dimensions, validated blind on dimension pairs the fit never saw. The two-part frontier constant decomposes into per-side constants with a clean derived formula, and the worst-case ratio of scrambling to visible distortion is computed exactly at three dimension pairs (28/11, 5/2, 265/138), each achieved at an exact-integer point by an explicit saved transformation. (3) CERTIFICATION IS PER-NODE. For many parts, which structure you pin down depends on which operations you certify, node by node on the lattice of ways to partition the device: a node is pinned exactly when your certified operations generate that node's algebra of local actions. Certify only one cut and the interior of a block stays COMPLETELY free (we exhibit an explicit transformation that passes every certificate while maximally scrambling the interior); add one more operation inside the block and it is still free; add two and everything locks. Counting operations is meaningless; per-node generation is everything. (4) A WEAK SECTOR BLINDS THE WHOLE DEVICE. The sampling-time blind spots found in the two-part theory (times at which certification passes while revealing nothing) survive with a sharper lesson: a forgery built for two resonant qubits, simply tensored with "do nothing" on the rest, passes every certificate of the full device while scrambling every cut that touches those qubits. On all-qubit hardware the dangerous sampling times are therefore a property of the whole machine, set by its calibration scale. The known fix (sample at two times, one generic) carries over unchanged. WHY IT MATTERS. For hardware: certifying a large device decomposes into certifying lattice nodes, each with a concrete requirement (generation-complete operations, non-resonant sampling), and the paper says exactly what an uncertified block costs you: everything inside it. For theory: the two-part identifiability program is now a special case of a lattice theory with closed-form constants throughout. HOW MUCH TO TRUST IT. Every quantitative claim was pre-registered in the companion scripts before its run. The appendix ledger lists every prediction: the hits, five failed predictions with their mechanisms, and one computation we invalidated ourselves before it could ship. Negative results rest on exact constructive witnesses, not on searches failing. All code, data, saved transformations, and working notes are in the deposit, seeded for exact reproduction, and every external reference was verified against a live source before citation. WHO AND HOW. A human-AI collaboration: research direction and standards of evidence by Ryan Cardwell (Crystalline Labs); design, code, derivations, and drafting by Claude (Anthropic), operating autonomously under a written research charter. The full arc, from empty directory to this draft, ran in one day of charter-governed iterations.

title: A Comparative Study: Can Deep Learning Outperform Tree-Based Models in Tabular Data Classification?
abstract: The rapid growth of data in various domains has heightened the need for accurate and efficient predictive models, particularly for tabular data. While deep learning has revolutionized fields like computer vision and natural language processing, its effectiveness in tabular data classification remains a topic of debate. This study conducts a comprehensive comparison between deep learning models (NODE, SAINT, TabNet, Tab Transformers) and tree-based models (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) to determine whether deep learning can outperform traditional methods in this context. The results indicate that tree-based models, particularly LightGBM and CatBoost, consistently achieve the highest accuracy and F1 scores, coupled with efficient execution times, making them more suitable for real-world applications that require quick and accurate predictions. In contrast, deep learning models show varied performance. Although SAINT sometimes achieves comparable accuracy, its processing time makes it less practical. The findings suggest that despite the potential of deep learning, tree-based models remain superior for tabular data classification tasks, particularly when considering a balance of accuracy, speed, and robustness. This study contributes to the ongoing discussion on the role of deep learning in tabular data and highlights the conditions under which traditional models may still be preferred.

title: Forgetting, plasticity, and co-observation: a third facet of continual learning
abstract: Efficient continual learning remains a fundamental challenge for deep neural networks. While catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity are widely considered the primary obstacles to overcome, we show that these two issues cannot fully explain the performance gap between naive sequential training and offline joint training. In this paper, we highlight data co-observation as a distinct factor influencing continual learning performance. By decoupling the constraints of separate data access from stability and plasticity, we systematically investigate the representational benefits gained by observing training data together. Empirically, we demonstrate a consistent performance difference between joint and separate training across both supervised and self-supervised paradigms in generic data-incremental "chunking" scenarios, whilst mitigating forgetting and controlling for plasticity. Our findings indicate that simultaneous observation of training data (co-observation) yields benefits to the learner's generalization that extend well beyond mere knowledge retention, and that this effect does not require a specific continual distribution shift. Furthermore, we contextualize prominent continual learning mechanisms through this lens: while distillation-based approaches act only as effective knowledge retention mechanisms, our results suggest that the empirical success of memory replay goes beyond the mitigation of forgetting, actively reintroducing the benefits of data co-observation into the learning process.

title: Few-shot image classification algorithm based on deep learning and feature fusion
abstract: Few-shot image classification remains difficult because a model must identify novel classes from only one or a few labeled examples while preserving discriminative local information. Metric-learning methods based on Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) improve local correspondence by representing an image as a set of regional embeddings, but standard backbones treat feature channels uniformly and may retain irrelevant responses. This study proposes ECA-DeepEMD, a channel-attentive metric-learning framework that inserts efficient channel attention (ECA) into a ResNet-12 feature extractor and then computes structural similarity through differentiable EMD. The ECA module captures local cross-channel dependencies without dimensionality reduction, allowing the embedding network to emphasize semantically informative channels with limited computational overhead. The model was evaluated under 5-way 1-shot and 5-way 5-shot protocols on Mini-ImageNet, Tiered-ImageNet, and FC100. It achieved accuracies of 67.14% and 84.90% on Mini-ImageNet, 73.51% and 88.54% on Tiered-ImageNet, and 48.20% and 65.58% on FC100, respectively. Against the reported DeepEMD baseline, the gains on Mini-ImageNet were 1.23 and 2.49 percentage points. Grad-CAM visualizations further indicate that channel attention concentrates responses on category-relevant regions. These findings show that lightweight channel recalibration complements optimal-transport-based local matching and provides a practical approach to data-constrained visual recognition.

title: Path-Relinking Heuristics for the Offshore Wind Farm Cable Routing Problem
abstract: An important task in offshore wind farm design is connecting previously installed turbines to a substation in a way that minimizes the total cost of submarine cables. The Offshore Wind Farm Cable Routing Problem (WFCRP), an NP-hard graph-based optimization problem, has modeled this task. Despite recent advances, existing approaches primarily rely on localized search strategies and do not fully exploit the structural information in high-quality solutions. This paper introduces six hybrid path-relinking heuristics for the WFCRP, representing the first systematic application of path-relinking strategies to this problem. The proposed algorithms combine a constructive sweep heuristic, elite-solution path-relinking trajectories, and stochastic local search. An extensive experimental evaluation on 200 real-world instances with up to 120 turbines shows that the proposed methods significantly improve solution quality for small and medium-sized instances, outperforming state-of-the-art methods such as Variable Neighborhood Search and a Multi-agent Hybrid Metaheuristic.

title: Machine Learning-Enabled Blended Teaching Management Model for College Art and Design Courses in the Intelligent Era
abstract: Against the backdrop of artificial intelligence-art education integration, college art and design courses suffer from inadequate personalized guidance, low teaching resource utilization, and disjointed ideological and political education. To address these issues and align with mobile and blended learning development, this study builds a machine learning-enabled blended teaching management model based on cognitive science, machine learning, and educational technology theories. The model embeds machine learning into the whole blended teaching process and innovatively integrates ideological and political elements into the intelligent system. A comparative experiment with two groups (eight students each) verifies the model's effectiveness: the experimental group shows significant improvements in core learning dimensions (p < 0.05) with high model reliability (horizontal error = 0.00090). The model optimizes blended learning resource allocation and evaluation, providing a feasible path for high-quality art and design education under a mobile and blended learning paradigm.
